claude.sample_unit: LLM-generated answers to simulated patient questions

links.outcome: Radiologist sensitivity for detecting deficient LLM answers to patient questions about radiology reports
links.effect: Individual sensitivity 81.4% to 96.5%; readers missed 5.6-11.1% of clinically significant errors; single reader missed avg 12.4% of deficiencies.
links.quote: For clinically significant errors, readers missed 5.6-11.1% of cases.

links.outcome: Whether clinician review catches errors in LLM patient-facing answers, single vs multi-reader
links.effect: Single reader missed an average of 12.4% of deficiencies; dual-reader review reduced average miss rate to 0.6%; triple-reader detected all.
links.quote: A single reader missed an average of 12.4% of deficiencies, whereas dual-reader review reduced the average miss rate to 0.6%; triple-reader review detected all deficiencies.

links.outcome: Miss rate of deficiencies with second reader review versus single reader
links.effect: Dual-reader review cut average miss rate from 12.4% (single) to 0.6%; triple-reader review detected all deficiencies.
links.quote: Dual-reader oversight significantly improves the safety and reliability of LLM-based communication tools.
Across all deficiencies, individual reader sensitivity ranged from 81.4% (95% CI, 73.3-87.5) to 96.5% (95% CI, 91.3-98.6), with significant differences (McNemar p < 0.001).

links.effect: Single reader missed average 12.4%; dual-reader review reduced miss rate to 0.6%; triple-reader review detected all deficiencies.
links.quote: A single reader missed an average of 12.4% of deficiencies, whereas dual-reader review reduced the average miss rate to 0.6%; triple-reader review detected all deficiencies.

links.effect: 113/1200 (9.4%) deficient; 18 clinically significant errors (1.5%); 95 incomplete/ambiguous responses (7.9%).
links.quote: Of 1200 answers, 113 (9.4%) were deficient by consensus, including 18 clinically significant errors (1.5%) and 95 incomplete/ambiguous responses (7.9%).

links.effect: For clinically significant errors, readers missed 5.6-11.1% of cases.

links.quote: Individual radiologist review of LLM-generated patient communications showed variable sensitivity, with some clinically significant errors remaining undetected.
